claims.text: AlCoFeNi annealed at about 1000 °C is predominantly single-phase ordered B2.
The high-temperature-annealed AlCoFeNi baseline has a coercive field of approximately 4 Oe.
Replacing approximately half of the Co in AlCoFeNi with Cr and annealing near 600 °C for 15 hours will induce fine-scale phase decomposition.
The Cr-substituted alloy will form a hierarchical microstructure consisting of a continuous B2 matrix and fine BCC or disordered precipitates.
The fine precipitates produced by the intervention will be enriched in Cr.
Cr-rich precipitates will disrupt ferromagnetic exchange.
The heterogeneous B2/BCC microstructure will provide pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
Co is ferromagnetic whereas the substituted Cr is antiferromagnetic in the relevant Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni alloy.
Substitution of Co by Cr reduces the overall ferromagnetic exchange interactions.
Cr substitution increases the density of chemically frustrated or ordered regions.
Fine Cr-rich microstructural inhomogeneities raise the energy barrier for magnetization reversal by enhancing domain-wall pinning.
Replacing part of the Co with Cr will increase the coercive field of AlCoFeNi-based alloy.
The intervention will increase coercivity from a few Oe to several tens of Oe relative to the baseline.
The coercivity increase should occur when the composition and processing yield a two-phase or hierarchical structure.
Excessive Cr content or aggressive heat treatment may produce excessive phase separation or brittle intermetallic phases.
Excessive phase separation or brittle intermetallic formation may offset the anticipated magnetic-performance improvement.

contradictions.description: The stated baseline is AlCoFeNi annealed at about 1000 °C, but the experiment anneals both baseline and modified alloys at 600 °C for 15 hours. Thus the proposed matched comparator is not the same baseline used for the stated approximately 4 Oe value and predicted few-Oe-to-tens-of-Oe change.

The conditions say that the alloy should remain compositionally homogeneous, whereas the proposed mediator requires phase decomposition and Cr enrichment of precipitates, which are forms of compositional heterogeneity.
